title: In situ structures of plant photosystem supercomplexes.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Fetched the RCSB (Protein Data Bank) entry metadata for 9XK3: released, linked to this paper, EMD-66946, 2.7 Å, 173,752 particles. Listed both Zenodo records via API: 13346121 is code plus a 560 MB source-data zip from a different, earlier energy-transfer paper; 13283796 is a single 8.8 KB Python simulation script. Europe PMC supplement endpoint returned no zip.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The full list of roughly 15 PDB and EMDB (Electron Microscopy Data Bank) entries (PSII-LHCII composite, protomers, dimers, trimer, tetramer, PSI-LHCI(-LHCII)) comes from the data availability statement; I did not open each entry or the density maps. Contents of Supplementary Tables 1–8 not seen.

a1_downloadable.note: PDB coordinates and EMDB maps are public; checked that 9XK3 resolves on RCSB.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No table with a prediction target exists; the outputs are atomic models and density maps of a few complexes. Any label (e.g. energy-transfer rate) would have to be computed by simulation, not read from a column.

a3_inputs_present.note: Coordinates and sequences are inside the PDB files (checked metadata only).

a4_units_stated.note: Not applicable in tabular sense; PDB/EMDB formats have standard units (Å).

a5_enough_rows.note: About 15 deposited structures per the paper text; far below 400 items for any learning task. Exact count of entries not verified one by one.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: under 1 GB for coordinates; maps larger, not checked
a6_fits_laptop.note: Coordinates are small; not the limiting factor.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Entry 9XK3 matches the paper's stated accession and citation; others not checked.

a8_label_provenance.note: The only quantitative per-structure outputs beyond geometry are energy-transfer rates from the authors' physics calculations (Zenodo code), i.e. model outputs computed from the structures themselves.

integration.partner_dataset: PDB / EMDB photosystem entries from other species (e.g. 5XNL pea, 5ZJI maize) cited in the paper
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Not formulated: a handful of structures supports structural comparison, not a learned model.

honest_claim_h3: No ML claim is supportable: the data is about 15 cryo-EM (cryo-electron microscopy) structures of photosystem complexes from one species, rice, with no measured per-item label.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use native photosystem structures to predict how efficiently light energy moves between pigment-protein units.
plain_idea.train_on: Atomic models of photosystem supercomplexes from rice chloroplasts; about 15 deposited structures (count from paper text, not verified individually).
plain_idea.predict: Energy-transfer rates between antenna units, which here come only from the authors' physics simulations, not from a direct measurement per structure.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Photosynthesis researchers would value fast efficiency estimates for new antenna arrangements, but this dataset is far too small and its labels are simulated.

label_elsewhere.why: Not assessed because Part A failed.

ml_idea: None viable: a structural biology paper whose deposits are ~15 PDB/EMDB entries with no label table; any target would be simulated energy-transfer rates (A8 circular).

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; rejected at Part A.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count deposited structures (≈15) — already kills it.

verdict_reason: Cryo-EM structure paper: about 15 PDB/EMDB entries from one species, no label column (A2), far too few items (A5), and the only quantitative outputs are simulated energy-transfer rates (A8).
